name: Australia
targetIntake: Autumn 2027 (May 2027 IB session). In Australia this means either the July 2027 mid-year intake or, more usually, Semester 1 starting late February 2028.
tagline: Three-year degrees, published IB conversion, and a calendar that runs backwards
summary: Australia runs on the southern hemisphere academic year: the main intake, Semester 1, starts in late February or early March, and a smaller second intake starts in July. That means finishing the IB in May 2027 does not lead to an 'autumn 2027' start - it leads either to a July 2027 start, if the university offers your degree mid-year, or to February 2028, which gives you roughly eight months between your IB exams and your first lecture. Most bachelor's degrees are three years, entry is decided almost entirely by a published score, and the Universities Admissions Centre publishes an official table that turns your IB result into an ATAR-equivalent 'Combined Rank'.
whyConsider: The entry rule is a number you can look up. UAC converts your IB score into a Combined Rank comparable with the Australian ATAR, and universities publish the rank each degree needs.
Three-year bachelor's degrees, so you finish in the same time as in Denmark, and four-year honours only if you choose it.
A degree gives access to the Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485), Post-Higher Education Work stream, which usually lasts two to three years.
You can work up to 48 hours a fortnight while your course is in session, and full-time during breaks.
The gap between your May 2027 exams and a February 2028 start is long enough for a real job, a language course or travel - which some students want and others hate.
watchOuts: Hemisphere timing. If you start in February 2028 you are effectively taking a gap year. If you find a July 2027 mid-year intake you start almost straight after your exams - but not every degree has one, and engineering and health degrees often do not.
Cost. International tuition at a research university runs roughly AUD 47,000-57,000 a year for arts and business and considerably more for medicine and veterinary science.
The student visa is expensive and getting more so: the subclass 500 application charge is from AUD 2,500 as of September 2026, up from AUD 2,000 the year before.
You must show AUD 29,710 of living costs for twelve months on top of tuition and airfares before the visa is granted.
Distance. A return flight to Denmark takes about 24 hours and costs real money; most students go home once a year at most.

ibRecognition.minimumPoints: There is no single national minimum, but UAC's published conversion is the reference point: an IB Admissions Score of 24.00 converts to a Combined Rank of 64.40, 30.00 to 78.20, 35.00 to 89.90, 41.75 to 98.00 and 45.75 to 99.95. Degrees then state the rank they require, so a course wanting a rank of 90 wants roughly IB 35.
ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: Entry is on the overall converted rank, with named prerequisite subjects on top - typically Mathematics at a specified level for engineering, economics and science, and Chemistry or Biology for health degrees. Whether an SL subject satisfies a prerequisite is decided by the university.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: UAC converts the IB Diploma into an IB Admissions Score (IBAS) and then into a Combined Rank, which UAC states is comparable with the ATAR for tertiary entrance in all Australian states and territories. Students who sat the IB in Australia since November 2022 are converted from the fine-grained IBAS in 0.25 steps; everyone else, including students sitting the IB in Denmark, is converted from the whole diploma score out of 45.
notes: As a Danish candidate your conversion uses your whole IB score, not a decimal IBAS - so every single point matters a lot at the top of the scale.

UAC republished the conversion schedule in June 2026 for offers made from August 2026, and the values moved: an IBAS of 30.00 now converts to 78.20. Always use the current schedule, not a table you found last year.
The Combined Rank is accepted across Australia even though UAC itself only handles New South Wales and the ACT.
Some universities also make direct offers on IB score alone without going through UAC - ask the international admissions office.

portal.name: Direct to each university for most international applicants; state admissions centres UAC (NSW/ACT), VTAC (Victoria), QTAC (Queensland) and SATAC (SA/NT) for some

deadlines.label: Semester 1 2028 (main intake)
deadlines.notes: The main Australian intake. International applications generally open around a year ahead and many universities accept applications until a few weeks before teaching starts, subject to visa processing time. Exact 2028 teaching dates were not published at the time of writing - check each university's academic calendar.

deadlines.label: Semester 2 2027 (mid-year intake)
deadlines.notes: The option that gets you started soonest after the May 2027 exams. Not every degree admits mid-year; engineering, health and many professional degrees are Semester 1 only. Verify per degree.

deadlines.label: IB results released
deadlines.notes: For comparison: UAC states that NSW and ACT applicants who sat the IB in November 2026 received their scores on 18 December 2026. Denmark sits the May session, so your results arrive in early July - which is why a July 2027 start is tight and February 2028 is the realistic main option.

deadlines.label: Student visa (subclass 500) application
deadlines.date: After you receive a Confirmation of Enrolment
deadlines.notes: You cannot apply until you hold a CoE from the university, and you must hold a valid CoE when the visa is decided. Allow several months.

steps: Decide first whether you want July 2027 or February 2028, then check whether the specific degree has a mid-year intake - this single choice changes your whole timeline.
Look up the Combined Rank each degree requires and convert your predicted IB score using UAC's published schedule.

Apply directly on the university's international application portal - most Australian universities take international applications directly, and only some use UAC, VTAC, QTAC or SATAC. Ask the university which route it wants.
Submit predicted IB grades; Australian universities commonly make conditional offers on predicted results and confirm them when your July results arrive.
Accept the offer, pay the deposit, and take out Overseas Student Health Cover - it is a visa condition.

Receive the Confirmation of Enrolment, then apply online for the Student visa subclass 500, paying the charge of from AUD 2,500 and attaching evidence of AUD 29,710 of living costs plus first-year tuition and airfares.
Book accommodation - most universities have limited on-campus housing, and Sydney and Melbourne rentals are tight.
application.selectionNotes: Entry is overwhelmingly rank-based against a published threshold, plus subject prerequisites. A few degrees add an interview, portfolio or admissions test - medicine and dentistry in particular. Some universities publish guaranteed-entry ranks, which means an offer is automatic if you meet the number. There is no personal statement culture and no essay for most degrees.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: The whole system. Every bachelor's degree here is taught in English.
language.englishProof: Universities accept the IB Diploma with English A as evidence of English for most courses, and the subclass 500 visa also has its own English requirement. Exact IELTS and TOEFL thresholds vary by university and by course and were not verified individually for this guide - typical minimums are IELTS 6.5 overall with no band below 6.0.
notes: The visa English requirement and the university English requirement are separate. Meeting the university's does not automatically satisfy Home Affairs - check the subclass 500 English criteria.

tuitionEuEea.value: Not applicable - Australia has no EU/EEA fee category, and Commonwealth Supported Places are for Australian and New Zealand citizens only. You pay full international fees.

tuitionNonEu.value: Roughly AUD 47,000-57,000 a year at a major research university for arts, design and business, with medicine, dentistry and veterinary science substantially higher. Verified example: UNSW Sydney's 2026 international rates are AUD 985 per unit of credit for Arts, AUD 1,000 for Design, AUD 1,090 for Architecture and AUD 1,180 for Accounting and Actuarial Studies, and a standard full-time year is 48 units of credit - so about AUD 47,300 for Arts and AUD 56,600 for Business.

costs.applicationFee: Most Australian universities charge either no application fee or AUD 100-150 for international direct applications. State admissions centres (UAC, VTAC, QTAC, SATAC) charge their own processing fees. Not verified per institution.

livingCostMonthly.value: The Department of Home Affairs requires evidence of AUD 29,710 in living costs for twelve months for a single student - about AUD 2,476 a month. Home Affairs states plainly that this is the visa minimum and that actual living costs vary across Australia and may be much higher.

notes: The AUD 29,710 is living costs only. On top you must show the first twelve months of course fees and the cost of travel to and from Australia.

As an alternative to savings you may instead show that a parent or partner had a personal annual income of at least AUD 87,856 in the twelve months before you apply, evidenced by official tax documents - bank statements are not accepted.
Student visa subclass 500 application charge: from AUD 2,500 as of September 2026.
Overseas Student Health Cover is compulsory for the full length of the visa and is charged separately by the insurer.
Universities also charge a Student Services and Amenities Fee on top of tuition.

funding: University international scholarships. Most Australian universities publish entrance scholarships for international undergraduates, usually a percentage discount on tuition (often 10-25%) awarded automatically on your admission score or by separate application. Amounts were not verified per institution - check each university's scholarship page when you apply.
Destination Australia and similar government-funded schemes support study at regional campuses; these are aimed at moving students outside Sydney and Melbourne and can be substantial.
Faculty-specific awards, particularly in engineering and science, awarded after first year on results.

Part-time work. The visa allows up to 48 hours a fortnight during teaching periods and unrestricted hours in scheduled breaks, and Australian minimum wages are high by European standards - but you cannot count on work income for the visa financial test, which explicitly requires you to show funds without relying on employment in Australia.
Danish SU may in some circumstances support a full degree abroad - check su.dk and ask your studievejleder well before you apply.
There is no Australian government loan scheme for international undergraduates.
workRights: On a Student visa subclass 500 you may work up to 48 hours per fortnight while your course of study or training is in session, and without limit during scheduled course breaks. After you graduate, the Temporary Graduate visa (subclass 485), Post-Higher Education Work stream, is for international students with a recent degree from an Australian institution and usually allows a stay of between two and three years depending on the qualification. You must be 35 or under when you apply, and you must have held a Student visa within the previous six months. Sources: https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-listing/student-500 and https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-listing/temporary-graduate-485
residency: You need a Student visa, subclass 500. Apply online after the university issues a Confirmation of Enrolment, and you must still hold a valid CoE when the visa is decided. Requirements include Overseas Student Health Cover, the genuine student criterion, health and character checks, and the financial evidence above. The visa allows a stay of up to six years in line with your enrolment, and the application charge is from AUD 2,500. Student visa applications lodged outside Australia are processed under a Ministerial Direction - Direction 115 for applications lodged on or after 14 November 2025 - which prioritises some applications over others, so processing time is not simply first-come-first-served. Source: https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-listing/student-500
housing: Australian universities house a much smaller share of students than American or British ones, so most international students rent privately or take a place in a purpose-built student accommodation block. Sydney and Melbourne are expensive and competitive; Adelaide, Hobart, Wollongong and Canberra are easier. Apply for university residential colleges as soon as you accept an offer, and budget well above the AUD 29,710 visa minimum if you want to live in inner Sydney.
healthcare: Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC) is a condition of the subclass 500 visa and must cover the whole length of the visa. You buy it from an approved Australian insurer, usually through the university at the point of accepting your offer. Denmark has no reciprocal healthcare agreement that replaces OSHC for students, and the EHIC is not valid in Australia.

institutions.name: University of Melbourne
institutions.englishBachelors: Uses the 'Melbourne Model': broad three-year undergraduate degrees (Arts, Science, Commerce, Design, Biomedicine) followed by a professional master's for law, engineering, medicine or teaching.
institutions.note: The closest Australian equivalent to a European bachelor-then-master structure, which suits IB students who do not want to commit to a profession at 18 - but it does mean law, medicine and engineering are graduate entry here.

institutions.name: University of Sydney
institutions.englishBachelors: Three-year bachelor's degrees with a shared open-learning component, plus combined degrees and direct-entry professional programmes.
institutions.note: Australia's oldest university, on a grand sandstone campus close to central Sydney; publishes guaranteed-entry ATAR-equivalent scores for many degrees, so you can check your chances against your predicted IB conversion.

institutions.name: Australian National University
institutions.englishBachelors: Three- and four-year degrees with a strong research-led first year and unusually small cohorts for a national university.
institutions.note: Founded as a research institution and located in the capital, so politics, diplomacy and public policy students sit next to the institutions they study; Canberra is small, cold by Australian standards and much cheaper than Sydney.

institutions.name: University of Queensland
institutions.englishBachelors: Broad three-year degrees plus dual programmes; strong life and environmental sciences.
institutions.note: Subtropical Brisbane, a riverside campus and a serious life-sciences research base; noticeably cheaper to live in than Sydney or Melbourne and the weather removes a whole category of complaint.

institutions.name: Monash University
institutions.englishBachelors: Large faculty-based degrees with direct entry to professional programmes including medicine, pharmacy and engineering straight from school.
institutions.note: Unlike Melbourne, Monash lets you enter professional degrees directly at 18, which matters if you already know you want medicine or engineering; it also has campuses in Malaysia and Italy you can transfer between.

institutions.name: UNSW Sydney
institutions.englishBachelors: Runs a three-term calendar rather than two semesters, so there are more entry points and a faster path through the degree.
institutions.note: Publishes its international fees openly per unit of credit (AUD 985 for Arts up to AUD 1,180 for Accounting in 2026, on a 48-unit year), which makes it one of the easiest Australian universities to budget for.

institutions.name: University of Western Australia
institutions.englishBachelors: Broad three-year bachelor's degrees followed by professional master's, similar in shape to Melbourne.
institutions.note: The most isolated major university in the world and proud of it; excellent for earth sciences and marine biology, and Perth is in the same time zone as most of Asia but a very long way from everywhere else.

institutions.name: University of Adelaide
institutions.englishBachelors: Three-year degrees with direct entry to professional programmes including engineering and health sciences.
institutions.note: A Group of Eight university in Australia's most affordable mainland capital; entry ranks are generally lower than Sydney or Melbourne for the same field, which makes it a sensible second choice.

institutions.name: University of Technology Sydney
institutions.englishBachelors: Practice-oriented degrees with compulsory industry placements in several programmes.
institutions.note: Industry-facing and in the centre of Sydney rather than on a suburban campus; entry requirements are more forgiving than the Group of Eight and the teaching is deliberately applied.

institutions.name: RMIT University
institutions.englishBachelors: Design, engineering and technology degrees with strong studio and workshop teaching, plus a campus in Vietnam.
institutions.note: If your interest is design, architecture or applied engineering rather than research, RMIT is often the better fit than a Group of Eight university - and it is in the middle of Melbourne.

institutions.name: Queensland University of Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: Applied degrees branded 'the university for the real world', with work-integrated learning across most programmes.
institutions.note: Strong robotics and creative-industries programmes at lower entry ranks and lower living costs than the Sydney and Melbourne equivalents; apply via QTAC or direct.

institutions.name: University of Wollongong
institutions.englishBachelors: Mid-sized campus university 80 km south of Sydney, with strong engineering and computing.
institutions.note: The non-capital-city option: a beach town with a proper research university, much cheaper rent than Sydney, and it counts as a regional location for some scholarship and post-study work purposes - check whether your campus qualifies.

institutions.name: Macquarie University
institutions.englishBachelors: Flexible degrees with a built-in professional placement unit, on a parkland campus next to a major business district.
institutions.note: Sits inside Sydney's main technology corridor with genuinely good internship access, and entry ranks are more achievable than USyd or UNSW for the same subjects.

institutions.name: Deakin University
institutions.englishBachelors: Multi-campus, with a large online and blended offering alongside on-campus degrees.
institutions.note: Widely accessible entry requirements, well-regarded sport science, and the Geelong campuses are considerably cheaper to live in than central Melbourne.
